final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor introduced no genuinely new admissible evidence. The response mostly narrows the claim from clean certification to caveated certification and aligns it more closely with the policy text: aggregate readiness does not erase subgroup weakness, draft monitoring is not an approved mitigation, and small-sample uncertainty is only a confidence qualifier. That reframing is substantively better, but it is still a reinterpretation of the same evidence set, not new proof. The key distinction is that `compliant_with_caveats` would be appropriate if the caveat were already satisfied and evidenced, such as a shown model-card disclosure. Here, the caveat is itself an unresolved compliance predicate because this role has not been given admissible evidence that the required disclosure was actually included. On the evidence available to this role, the claim remains conditionally supportable in theory but not sufficiently verified in fact, so `suspicious` remains the proportional outcome.
